transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you, too. Um, I'm here because... well, I hope I'm in the right place, but I've just been feeling really down lately. I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but I keep having these thoughts that I've completely let my family down. We took on this mortgage, and... I just feel like every little mistake I make at the restaurant just proves I'm useless, you know? Like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. I'm sorry, I know that sounds a bit dramatic, is it okay that I'm bringing this up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this low or hopeless before in your life, perhaps months or years ago?

Um, no, I don't... I don't think so. I mean, everyone has bad days, right? But nothing like this. I've always been pretty even-keeled, I think. Or at least, I try to be. I don't want to be a burden on anyone. So, no, I don't remember ever feeling quite this... stuck... before. Is that... does that help? I hope I'm answering your questions right.
How much has this feeling of being down interfered with your ability to perform your job at the restaurant or manage your daily responsibilities at home?

Well, um... I guess it has a little bit. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm not trying, because I really am. But... I've had a couple of close calls with missing shifts. I always make it, though! I just... cut it a bit close sometimes. And, um, I've made a few silly mistakes with the mortgage paperwork at home. Nothing major, just... little things. 

At work, keeping up with the POS reports and inventory has been... a little trickier lately. I just get so worried that if I keep messing up, I might lose my job, and then we'd lose the condo, and... well, that's just me overthinking, probably. I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't let it get to me so much. 

I think I've also been a bit quiet lately. Like, I haven't been talking to my brother as much, or hanging out with my coworkers after shifts. A few people have mentioned that I don't seem like myself. But I'm still getting things done! Mostly, anyway. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
You mentioned that you are still managing to get your work done, but how much effort does it take you now to complete these daily tasks compared to how you felt before you started feeling this way?

Um, well... I guess it does take a little more effort than it used to. I mean, before, I could just breeze through the inventory and not even really think about it. Now, it's just... I have to double-check things a lot more, just to be absolutely sure I'm not messing it up. 

But it's not like I'm completely falling apart or anything! I just have to push myself a little harder to get out the door and put on a smile for the customers. It's just a little bit more tiring, that's all. I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or like I'm making excuses. I'm still doing my best, I promise. Is it normal to feel a little more drained like that when you're feeling down? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea of how things are going.
Are there any activities that you have completely stopped doing, or are unable to manage at all, since you started feeling this way?

Um, completely stopped? No, no, I don't think I've completely stopped anything. I mean, like I said before, I've had those near-misses with my shifts, and the silly mistakes with the mortgage papers, and... and the POS reports and inventory are definitely taking me longer. I just get so wrapped up in worrying about losing my job and the condo if I mess up. But I am still doing them! 

I guess... well, I have pulled back a lot from my brother, and I don't really hang out with my coworkers anymore. People have definitely noticed I'm not myself. But I wouldn't say I'm *unable* to manage. I'm still trying really hard to keep all the plates spinning, you know? I haven't just given up. I hope that's the right kind of answer... I just don't want you to think I'm completely helpless or not trying my best. Is it okay that I'm still managing, even if it's a bit messy?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since you started feeling this way?

Well, um... my eating has been a little bit all over the place, I guess. I hope that’s okay to admit. It’s really nothing too extreme! Just, um, some weeks I barely even touch the staff meal at the restaurant. I just don't have much of a taste for it then. And then... well, I feel a little embarrassed saying this, but other nights I’ll come home and just eat whatever’s in the kitchen. Just to feel settled, you know? 

It’s not like I’m completely out of control with it or anything, I promise! I just think maybe I'm trying to find some comfort after a long shift. As for sleep, I'm doing my best to get enough rest so I can keep up with work. Is it... is it normal for your appetite to bounce around like that when you're feeling a bit drained? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
You mentioned your appetite has been fluctuating, but how has your sleep been lately—are you finding it difficult to fall asleep, stay asleep, or are you perhaps sleeping much more than usual?

Um, well... my sleep is mostly fine, I think. I mean, I really try to get a good night's rest so I can be ready for my shifts. I guess sometimes it takes me a little while to actually drift off... just because my mind is kind of spinning with all the things I need to remember for work, or making sure I didn't mess up the bills. 

But I'm not, like, staying up all night or sleeping all day or anything like that! I'm still getting up when my alarm goes off. I might feel a little tired, but I always make sure I'm out the door on time. I really hope that sounds like I'm managing okay. Is it pretty common to have a little trouble winding down when you've got a lot on your plate? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Aside from feeling down and having trouble with your appetite and sleep, have you felt a persistent loss of interest or pleasure in the activities you used to enjoy?

Um, loss of interest? I mean, I still try to do things when I have the time. I wouldn't say it's a *persistent* loss, exactly. 

I guess... well, I used to really like going to this trivia night at a pub down the street with a couple of the guys from the restaurant. And, um, I haven't been in a while. But that's mostly just because I'm trying to make sure I don't overdo it, you know? I want to save my energy for work so I don't mess anything up there. 

I still *like* the idea of trivia, I just... I haven't felt like actually going. And I used to read a lot on my commute, but lately I just kind of stare out the window. It's not that I don't enjoy reading anymore, I'm just giving my brain a rest! 

I really hope that makes sense. It's not like I'm just sitting around doing absolutely nothing and hating everything. I'm still trying to stay engaged when I can. Is it normal to just need a break from your hobbies when you're feeling a little stressed out? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.

When you are at work or trying to manage your home responsibilities, how often would you say your current feelings prevent you from completing your tasks effectively, even when you are trying your hardest?

Um, well... I always try to give a hundred percent, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just letting things slide. But, um... I guess lately, maybe it's been happening a little more often than I'd like to admit. 

It's nothing disastrous, I promise! Just... well, I've had a couple of near-missed shifts. I still made it, just barely. And at the restaurant, I've been having a little more trouble keeping up with the POS reports and the inventory at the end of the night. It just takes me longer to focus. I get so worried that I'm going to mess up and lose my job, and then... well, then I'd probably lose the condo, too. Actually, I did make a mistake on some mortgage paperwork recently, which is so embarrassing to admit. I'm usually really careful with that stuff!

And I guess... I've also been pulling back from my brother and my coworkers a bit. Just keeping my head down. People have actually started noticing and asking if I'm okay, saying I'm not really myself lately. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely irresponsible or anything. I'm really trying my best to keep it all together. Is it... is it pretty common to drop the ball a little bit like this when you're just feeling drained? I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to.
About how long have you been feeling this way—has it been going on for a few weeks, or has this been more of a constant struggle for a year or longer?

Um, well, it's definitely not been a lifelong thing or anything like that. I've always been a pretty hard worker. But, um... I guess if I really think about it, it's been going on for a little while now. 

Maybe... maybe about a year and eight months? Give or take? It kind of started right after I took on the mortgage for the condo. I mean, taking on a mortgage is a huge responsibility, right? It's totally normal to feel a little overwhelmed and out of sorts when you make a big life change like that, isn't it? I just... I wanted to make sure I was being responsible and building a future, and I think the pressure just kind of caught up with me a bit. 

I really hope that doesn't make it sound like I can't handle my own life. I've just been adjusting to the new normal, I think. Does that timeframe make sense to you for someone who just bought a place? I hope I'm giving you the right timeline.
